title.narrative: Right to Care V: Enhancing the Protection and wellbeing of conflict affected children through Strengthened Protection mechanisms and targeted assistance.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="color: black font-size: 8.5pt font-family: Roboto"gtStreet Child with its partner Protection Without Borders will strengthen community-based child protection mechanisms in ten communities of Bama, Damboa, Dikwa, Pulka- Gwoza and Monguno in Borno State, in order to enhance protective environments of communities and address critical needs faced by the targeted 18,000 (out of the total of 1,973,047 projected within IPC Phase 3-5, CH 2023) vulnerable conflict affected children and caregivers lt/spangtltspan style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0) font-size: 8.5pt font-family: Roboto"gtdue to the impact of the food crisis which will increase the chances for many to adopt negative coping mechanisms such as selling their productive assets for short-term survival, begging or borrowing money to survive, recruitment to non-state armed groups or resorting to survival sex. Women and children are at particular risk and are often exposed to sexual and gender-based violence compounded by the lean season food crisis. A key challenge to address this situation is desperate lack of funding. If not addressed, the situation may deteriorate to emergency and famine like 522,366 people in Abadam and Guazamala who are projected to be in IPC Phase 4.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size: 11pt color: rgb(0, 0, 0) font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gt
lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size: 11pt color: rgb(0, 0, 0) font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtltspan style="font-size:8.5ptfont-family:Robotomso-bidi-font-family:Arial color:black"gtTo maximize experience, presence, and value for money concerns, the project will be implemented in 10 communities across the 5 LGAs (Bama, Monguno, Gwoza, Damboa, Dikwa) in partnership with Protection Without Borders ltspan style="mso-spacerun:yes"gt lt/spangt(POWIB) having added value lt/spangtltspan style="font-size:8.5ptfont-family:Robotocolor:blackmso-color-alt:windowtext background:white"gtto legal aspect of protection support, representation to victims of abuse, neglect and abuse related to GBV victims, children in contact with the law due to petty and grave offenses as result of negative coping mechanisms to remain afloat in their situationslt/spangtltspan style="font-size:8.5pt font-family:Robotomso-bidi-font-family:Arial"gt. These communities have been selected based on protection gaps identified within the Sector as well as the pre-existing child ltspan style="color:black"gtprotection infrastructure and community relationships built during previous protection interventions, that can be further strengthened and localized in line with allocating priorities of ensuring lt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-size:8.5ptfont-family:Roboto"gtChildren at risk (boys and girls) including adolescents, children with disabilities access preventive and comprehensive quality response services in a timely manner.lt/spangtltspan style="font-size:8.5ptfont-family:Robotomso-bidi-font-family: Arialcolor:black"gtltbrgt ltbrgt Protection Without Borders( POWIB) will conduct front-line protection activities, including the set-up and running of child-friendly spaces, case management systems and community awareness within communities of implementation to ensure that children have access to dedicated protective services including legal support, that improve psychosocial wellbeing as well as providing case management services to the most vulnerable children in coordination with relevant stakeholders. This direct service provision will be supported by capacity building of community and government child protection structures to empower communities with skills necessary to identify, mitigate and respond to child protection issues. In line with sector priorities, referral mechanisms and pathways will be mapped and strengthened through consistent engagement at sector level. ltbrgt ltbrgt Street Child will support Protection Without Borders through provision and capacity building of specialized protection services including family tracing and reunification (FTR) , case management and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) on basis of need. POWIB’s technical capacity building will be supported by institutional and organizational strengthening in key operational aspects including logistics and procurement, finance, internal policy, and ME frameworks/reporting mechanisms, and as part of mentorship throughout the implementation period. These strengthening initiatives will be implemented through a range of formats and modalities to best facilitate institutional learning - workshops and presentations will be followed up with bilateral monitoring and review. Key Street Child staff will carry out 1-1 mentoring with POWIB partners on a scheduled basis, either in field or ltspan style="mso-spacerun:yes"gt lt/spangtoffice. Capacity building topics will be primarily raised and requested by POWIB staff, to promote internal reflection. lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
